questions.q: Why shouldn't your application code parse Claude's narration text (like 'I'll check the weather now') to decide what action to take?
options: Because narration text is always empty in practice
Because Claude is not allowed to produce narration text
Because narration text is encrypted and cannot be read
Because the structured tool_use block and stop_reason are the reliable signal of what happened — wording can vary and shouldn't drive control flow
questions.explain: Claude may use various phrasings when explaining its actions; code should rely on the structured tool_use block and stop_reason, not specific text patterns.

questions.q: What does tool_choice: {"type": "auto"} do, and is it the default?
options: It blocks all tool calls; it is not the default
It forces exactly one specific named tool; it is not the default
It lets Claude decide whether to call any provided tool or respond directly; yes, it's the default when tools are provided
It requires the user to manually approve every tool call
questions.explain: auto is the default tool_choice setting when tools are present — Claude itself decides whether a tool call is warranted.

questions.q: What's the practical side effect of forcing tool use with tool_choice: {"type": "any"} or {"type": "tool", ...}?
options: It doubles the number of tokens billed for every request automatically
It pre-fills the assistant turn, so Claude will not emit narration text before the tool_use block, even if asked to
It disables the model's ability to call any tool at all
It has no effect on the response format whatsoever
questions.explain: Because any/tool pre-fill the assistant message to force a tool call, Claude skips natural-language commentary before the tool_use block on that turn.

questions.q: In the full two-turn exchange example, what has to be included in turn 2's messages besides the new tool_result?
options: Nothing else — only the tool_result needs to be sent
The original system prompt must be sent twice
The assistant's own prior tool_use content block, sent back as part of the conversation history
A brand new tools array with completely different tool definitions
questions.explain: The model needs its own earlier action (the tool_use block) back in context alongside the result, so it can make sense of what that result is actually answering.

questions.q: If you want Claude to both call a specific tool AND provide natural-language commentary in the same turn, what does this lesson recommend?
options: This is impossible under any circumstances
Always use tool_choice: {"type": "none"} instead
Use tool_choice: {"type": "auto"} and explicitly ask for the tool in the prompt, rather than forcing with "any" or "tool"
Send the request twice with two different tool_choice values simultaneously
questions.explain: Forcing with any/tool suppresses commentary by design; using auto plus an explicit instruction in the prompt lets Claude both narrate and still call the intended tool.
